_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Türkiye (Turkey) covering Hittites, Phrygians, Lydians, Greco-Roman (Ephesus, Constantinople), Byzantine Empire, Seljuk Turks, Ottoman Empire (1299-1922), WWI defeat, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's republic 1923, secularization, Kurdish conflict, military coups (1960/1971/1980/1997), EU accession talks, Erdoğan's AKP Islamist rule (2003+), 2016 coup attempt, Syrian refugee crisis, and authoritarian drift.

religion.note: Officially secular state (Atatürk legacy); Sunni Hanafi majority; Alevi (heterodox Shia-like, Anatolian, Bektashi Sufi influence); secular vs Islamist divide (AKP re-Islamized); Diyanet (state religious affairs); Armenian/Greek Orthodox (decimated by genocide/population exchanges); Jews (Sephardic, Istanbul)

ethnic_groups.name: Turkish
ethnic_groups.notes: 70-75% range; Turkic; Anatolian; Oghuz heritage; linguistic identity (Turkish language); Ottoman legacy; Black Sea/Aegean/Central Anatolia; nationalism strong; Kemalist/secular vs conservative divide

ethnic_groups.name: Kurdish
ethnic_groups.notes: 15-20% range; Kurdish language (suppressed historically, 'mountain Turks' denial); southeast (Diyarbakır, Van); PKK insurgency (1984+, ~40,000 dead); HDP party; Newroz; Alevi and Sunni; oppression-assimilation policies; Erdoğan alternated repression/outreach

ethnic_groups.name: Arab
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border (Hatay); Syrian refugees ~3.6M since 2011 (largest refugee host globally); Alawite Arabs in Hatay

ethnic_groups.name: Zaza
ethnic_groups.notes: 1-2% range; Iranian language; eastern Anatolia; distinct from Kurds but often grouped; mostly Alevi

ethnic_groups.name: Circassian
ethnic_groups.notes: North Caucasus; refugees from Russian conquest 1860s; Sunni Muslim; assimilated but distinct identity

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Armenian, Greek, Laz, Georgian, Bosniak, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: 2-3% range; Greeks/Armenians decimated (1915 genocide, 1923 population exchange); Laz (Black Sea, Georgian-related); Bosniak/Pomak Muslims; Hemsheni Armenians (Islamized)

independence.from: Successor to Ottoman Empire (dissolved after WWI); Republic declared by Atatürk

country_profile.notes_unique: Only country spanning two continents (3% Europe, 97% Asia, Bosporus); successor to Ottoman Empire; Atatürk secularization (Latin script, women's rights, caliphate abolished 1924); Armenian Genocide 1915 (~1.5M, denied by state); Kurdish conflict (PKK, ~40,000 dead); NATO member (1952); EU candidate (since 1999, stalled); 2016 coup attempt (Fethullah Gülen blamed, 77,000+ arrested); Erdoğan's authoritarian turn; Hagia Sophia re-converted to mosque 2020; Syrian refugees 3.6M; inflation crisis 2021-23

current_leader.name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: AKP (Justice and Development Party, Islamist-rooted); PM 2003-14 then President; former Istanbul mayor; economic growth then crisis; authoritarian drift (jailed journalists, judges); 2016 coup attempt (purges); 2017 referendum (executive presidency); 2023 re-elected after earthquake; Ottoman nostalgia; Neo-Ottomanism; Hagia Sophia; Syria intervention; Libya; Azerbaijan support; S-400 (Russia, US tensions)

former_leaders.name: Abdullah Gül
former_leaders.notes: AKP; Erdoğan ally; moderate Islamist; wife wore headscarf (controversial in secular Turkey); EU accession talks

former_leaders.name: Ahmet Necdet Sezer
former_leaders.notes: Former Constitutional Court judge; secularist; clashed with AKP government

former_leaders.name: Süleyman Demirel
former_leaders.notes: Center-right; PM multiple times before presidency; 1997 'postmodern coup' (military forced Islamist PM Erbakan out)

former_leaders.name: Turgut Özal
former_leaders.notes: Economic liberalization; PM 1983-89; Kurdish opening; died in office (heart attack, poisoning rumors)

former_leaders.name: Kenan Evren
former_leaders.notes: General; led 1980 military coup; repression; 1982 constitution; later convicted of coup (2014)

former_leaders.name: Celal Bayar
former_leaders.notes: Democrat Party; ousted by 1960 military coup; death sentence commuted

former_leaders.name: Mustafa İsmet İnönü
former_leaders.notes: Atatürk's successor; WWII neutrality (until 1945); multi-party transition 1946; CHPleader

former_leaders.name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
former_leaders.notes: Founder of modern Turkey; War of Independence hero (Gallipoli, Sakarya); abolished caliphate; secularization; Latin alphabet; women's suffrage; died 1938 (cirrhosis); cult of personality; 'Father of Turks'

910.name: Ancient Anatolia and Hittite Empire
910.description: Anatolia as a cradle of civilization — from the world's oldest known settlement at Çatalhöyük through the great Hittite Empire, the Phrygian and Lydian kingdoms, and the invention of coinage.

sub_clusters.name: Çatalhöyük and Neolithic Anatolia
sub_clusters.description: Çatalhöyük as one of the world's first proto-urban settlements, Göbekli Tepe as the oldest known monumental structures, and the Neolithic revolution in Anatolia.
key_events: Göbekli Tepe constructed — world's oldest known monumental structures, predating agriculture (c. 9500 BC)
Çatalhöyük flourishes as a major Neolithic settlement of up to 10,000 people (c. 7500–5700 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Hittite Empire
sub_clusters.description: The Hittite Empire based at Hattusa — one of the great Bronze Age superpowers, their wars with Egypt, the world's first known peace treaty at Kadesh, and their mysterious collapse.
key_events: Battle of Kadesh and the Egyptian-Hittite peace treaty — the oldest known peace treaty (c. 1274 BC)
Hittite Empire collapses in the Bronze Age Collapse (c. 1178 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Phrygians, Lydians, and the Invention of Coinage
sub_clusters.description: The Phrygian kingdom of King Midas, the Lydian kingdom of Croesus, the invention of coined money that revolutionized commerce, and the Ionian Greek cities of the Aegean coast.
key_events: Lydians invent coined money — transforming global commerce (c. 600 BC)
Cyrus the Great conquers Lydia and Croesus (546 BC)

910.name: Classical and Roman Anatolia
910.description: Anatolia under Persian, Hellenistic, and Roman rule — Troy, Alexander's campaigns, the Hellenistic kingdoms of Pergamon and Pontus, and Roman Asia Minor's immense wealth.

sub_clusters.name: Persian and Hellenistic Anatolia
sub_clusters.description: Achaemenid rule over Anatolia, Alexander's crossing at the Hellespont, the successor kingdoms of Pergamon and Pontus, and the Library of Pergamon rivaling Alexandria.
key_events: Alexander the Great cuts the Gordian Knot at Gordium (333 BC)

sub_clusters.name: Roman Asia Minor
sub_clusters.description: Anatolia as the wealthiest region of the Roman Empire, the Seven Churches of Asia in Revelation, the spread of Christianity through Paul's missionary journeys, and the Council of Nicaea.
key_events: Council of Nicaea — first ecumenical council defining Christian orthodoxy, held in Anatolia (325 AD)

920.name: Byzantine Empire and Constantinople
920.description: Constantinople as the greatest city of the medieval world, the Byzantine Empire's millennium-long defense of Christendom, Justinian's golden age, and the Arab and Seljuk threats.

sub_clusters.name: Founding of Constantinople and Justinian
sub_clusters.description: Constantine's founding of Constantinople, the Hagia Sophia as the greatest building of the medieval world, Justinian's reconquests and legal codification, and the Arab sieges.
key_events: Constantine founds Constantinople — the 'New Rome' (330 AD)
Justinian builds the Hagia Sophia — the architectural wonder of the age (537 AD)

sub_clusters.name: Iconoclasm and Macedonian Renaissance
sub_clusters.description: The Iconoclast controversy, the Macedonian dynasty's cultural and military renaissance, Basil II's conquests, and the catastrophic defeat at Manzikert opening Anatolia to the Seljuk Turks.
key_events: Battle of Manzikert — Seljuk Turks defeat the Byzantines, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement (1071)

920.name: Seljuk Sultanate of Rum
920.description: The Turkification and Islamization of Anatolia under the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum, the synthesis of Persian, Turkish, and Byzantine cultures, Rumi's poetry, and the Mongol subjugation.

sub_clusters.name: Seljuk Anatolia and the Crusades
sub_clusters.description: The founding of the Sultanate of Rum at Konya, interactions with Crusader armies passing through, the flowering of Anatolian Seljuk architecture and madrasas, and Rumi's mystical poetry in Konya.
key_events: Jalal ad-Din Rumi settles in Konya, composing the Masnavi — one of the greatest works of mystical literature (c. 1244–1273)

sub_clusters.name: Mongol Subjugation and Beylik Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: The Battle of Köse Dağ reducing the Sultanate to a Mongol vassal, the disintegration into rival Turkish beyliks (principalities), and the emergence of the small Ottoman beylik in northwestern Anatolia.
key_events: Battle of Köse Dağ — Mongol victory ends Seljuk independence (1243)

930.name: Rise of the Ottoman Empire
930.description: The Ottoman transformation from a small frontier beylik into a world empire — the conquest of Constantinople, the age of Suleiman the Magnificent, and the empire's military and cultural zenith.

sub_clusters.name: Ottoman Founding and Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Osman I's beylik, the crossing into Europe, the Battle of Kosovo, the catastrophe of Ankara against Timur, recovery under Murad II, and the young Mehmed II's obsession with Constantinople.
key_events: Battle of Kosovo — Ottoman victory establishes dominance over the Balkans (1389)
Battle of Ankara — Timur defeats Bayezid I, nearly destroying the empire (1402)

sub_clusters.name: Fall of Constantinople
sub_clusters.description: Mehmed II's conquest of Constantinople — the event that ended the medieval world, the use of massive cannons, the transformation of Hagia Sophia into a mosque, and the birth of Istanbul as the new Ottoman capital.
key_events: Mehmed II conquers Constantinople — end of the Byzantine Empire and the medieval era (May 29, 1453)

sub_clusters.name: Suleiman the Magnificent
sub_clusters.description: The golden age under Suleiman — the empire's maximum extent from Hungary to Yemen, the codification of law (Kanuni), Sinan's architectural masterpieces, and Ottoman cultural brilliance.
key_events: Siege of Vienna — high-water mark of Ottoman expansion into Europe (1529)
Mimar Sinan builds the Süleymaniye Mosque — his Istanbul masterpiece (1550–1557)

930.name: Ottoman Decline and Reform
930.description: The long Ottoman decline — the Sultanate of Women, the failed siege of Vienna, military losses to Russia and Austria, and the early reform attempts from Selim III to Mahmud II.

sub_clusters.name: Stagnation and Military Decline
sub_clusters.description: The post-Suleiman decline, the Sultanate of Women, the failed 1683 siege of Vienna, the Treaty of Karlowitz ceding Hungary, and the growing Russian threat under Catherine the Great.
key_events: Second Siege of Vienna fails — beginning of Ottoman territorial retreat (1683)
Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca — Russia gains access to the Black Sea and right to protect Orthodox Christians (1774)

sub_clusters.name: Early Reforms and Janissary Abolition
sub_clusters.description: Selim III's Nizam-i Cedid new army, the Janissary revolt and his murder, Mahmud II's decisive destruction of the Janissary Corps, and the beginning of the Tanzimat modernization.
key_events: 'Auspicious Incident' — Mahmud II destroys the Janissary Corps (June 15, 1826)

940.name: Tanzimat and Constitutional Era
940.description: The Tanzimat modernization, the constitutional movements, the Young Turks' revolution, the catastrophic Balkan Wars, WWI, and the Armenian Genocide.

sub_clusters.name: Tanzimat Reforms and First Constitution
sub_clusters.description: The Gülhane Decree and Tanzimat reforms, the brief 1876 Constitution, Abdulhamid II's autocratic rule, the Russo-Turkish War of 1877–78, and the loss of Balkan territories.
key_events: Gülhane Decree launches the Tanzimat modernization program (1839)
Congress of Berlin — Ottoman Empire loses most of its European territories (1878)

sub_clusters.name: Young Turk Revolution and WWI
sub_clusters.description: The Young Turk Revolution restoring the constitution, the Balkan Wars, the Ottoman entry into WWI alongside Germany, the Gallipoli Campaign, and the Armenian Genocide.
key_events: Young Turk Revolution restores the Ottoman Constitution (1908)
Gallipoli Campaign — Ottoman victory over the Allies; Mustafa Kemal emerges as hero (1915–1916)
Armenian Genocide — mass killing and deportation of Armenians (1915–1923)

940.name: Turkish War of Independence and Republic
940.description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk's War of Independence against Allied-occupied Anatolia, the founding of the Turkish Republic, and the radical Kemalist reforms transforming society.

sub_clusters.name: War of Independence
sub_clusters.description: The Allied occupation and Greek invasion of Anatolia, Mustafa Kemal's organization of resistance in Ankara, the decisive Battle of Sakarya, the Great Offensive, and the Treaty of Lausanne.
key_events: Mustafa Kemal lands at Samsun — beginning of the national resistance (May 19, 1919)
Great Offensive — Turkish forces defeat the Greek army at Dumlupınar (August 1922)
Treaty of Lausanne recognizes the sovereignty of the Republic of Turkey (July 24, 1923)

sub_clusters.name: Kemalist Revolution
sub_clusters.description: The proclamation of the Republic, the abolition of the Caliphate, the adoption of Latin script and Western legal codes, secularization, women's suffrage, and Atatürk's transformation of Turkish society.
key_events: Republic of Turkey proclaimed with Ankara as capital (October 29, 1923)
Abolition of the Ottoman Caliphate (March 3, 1924)
Latin alphabet adopted, replacing Arabic script (1928)
Death of Atatürk (November 10, 1938)

950.name: Multi-Party Era and Military Interventions
950.description: Turkey's transition to multi-party democracy, the periodic military coups serving as 'guardians' of secularism, NATO membership, the Cyprus crisis, and the Kurdish conflict.

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Transition and NATO
sub_clusters.description: The transition to multi-party elections, the Democrat Party victory, Turkey's entry into NATO during the Korean War, and the 1960 military coup overthrowing Adnan Menderes.
key_events: Turkey joins NATO (1952)
1960 military coup — PM Adnan Menderes overthrown and later executed

sub_clusters.name: Coups, Cyprus, and Political Violence
sub_clusters.description: The 1971 'coup by memorandum,' the 1974 Cyprus invasion, the left-right political violence of the 1970s, and the devastating 1980 military coup under Kenan Evren.
key_events: Turkey invades Cyprus — Operation Attila divides the island (July 1974)
1980 military coup — the most comprehensive intervention in Turkish history

sub_clusters.name: PKK Conflict and 1997 'Postmodern Coup'
sub_clusters.description: The PKK Kurdish insurgency, Turgut Özal's economic liberalization, the military's 1997 'postmodern coup' against the Islamist Erbakan government, and the capture of PKK leader Öcalan.
key_events: PKK insurgency begins in southeastern Turkey (1984)
PKK leader Abdullah Öcalan captured in Kenya (1999)

960.name: AKP Era and Erdoğan
960.description: The rise of the AKP and Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Turkey's EU accession bid, the Gezi Park protests, the 2016 coup attempt, the transition to a presidential system, and Turkey's assertive foreign policy.

sub_clusters.name: AKP Rise and EU Bid
sub_clusters.description: The AKP's landslide victory, democratic reforms for EU accession, the Ergenekon trials against the 'deep state,' rapid economic growth, and the Gezi Park protests.
key_events: AKP wins parliamentary elections — Erdoğan becomes PM (2003)
Gezi Park protests sweep Turkey's major cities (May–June 2013)

sub_clusters.name: 2016 Coup Attempt and Presidential System
sub_clusters.description: The dramatic failed coup attempt of July 15, 2016, the massive post-coup purges, the constitutional referendum establishing a presidential system, and Erdoğan's consolidation of power.
key_events: Failed coup attempt — over 250 killed as military factions try to seize power (July 15, 2016)
Constitutional referendum transitions Turkey to a presidential system (April 2017)

sub_clusters.name: Regional Assertiveness and Contemporary Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Turkish military operations in Syria and Libya, the 2023 earthquake catastrophe, Erdoğan's re-election, the economic crisis with hyperinflation, and Turkey's balancing between NATO and Russia.
key_events: Devastating earthquakes in southeastern Turkey kill over 50,000 (February 6, 2023)
Erdoğan wins re-election in a competitive run-off (May 2023)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
